tokens.ship-progress:
### Progress Reporting (OpenCode)

OpenCode has no spex status line, so the pipeline reports its progress in the conversation. `"$SHIP_STATE" progress` is an additional state command: it reads the state file and prints a `BANNER` line (stage, progress bar, oversight level) and a `PLAN` line. Only the `BANNER` line is used here.

- Whenever the pipeline pauses (findings that need the user, blockers, retries exhausted), run `SHIP_STATE_FILE="$SHIP_STATE_FILE" "$SHIP_STATE" pause` first. Whenever a stage fails with an unrecoverable error, run `SHIP_STATE_FILE="$SHIP_STATE_FILE" "$SHIP_STATE" fail` first.
- After every state command that changes the pipeline (`create`, `advance`, `pause`, `fail`, `resume`, including the `resume` of `--resume`), run:
  ```bash
  SHIP_STATE_FILE="$SHIP_STATE_FILE" "$SHIP_STATE" progress
  ```
- Put the text after `BANNER ` verbatim as its own line in your next reply. Do not reword it or compose your own banner. Ignore the `PLAN` line.
- When `advance` prints `PIPELINE_COMPLETE`, the state file still exists with stage `done`: `advance` does not remove it, whatever the table and the paragraph above say, and only `cleanup` does. Run `progress` immediately, before the walkthrough draft and before anything removes the state file.
- When the user replies to a pause, run `progress` before continuing, even if you did not run `resume` yourself (the prompt hook may already have set the state back to running).
- If `progress` prints nothing, skip this step and continue. Progress reporting never blocks the pipeline.
